59785867.s: Edge of the World is a set of towering rocky heights overlooking a deep valley, a rare natural landmark shaped by time. The viewpoint dates back about 50 million years, when the area was the bed of a vast sea covering the Arabian Peninsula as far as the Levant. It shows traces of river channels and long-dry waterways that stretch for hundreds of kilometres and draw beautiful patterns across the broad plains, along with many kinds of fossils, sculpted forms and striking carvings formed by natural forces on the valley rocks, which tell of the conditions the region lived through and the successive eras it has seen.

59785762.s: Wadi Al Mishqar is one of the largest valleys of Sudair, with a length of more than 100 kilometres. It begins in the highlands near Al Majmaah and runs north-east past the Al Majmaah Dam and its palm farms, separating Harmah from Al Majmaah. It is known for its large trees and varied wild plants, especially in Rawdat Al Muzairaa at the head of the valley, and turns green after the spring rains.

59785620.s: Wadi Mawan is one of the valleys of Najd, located near the town of Al Dilam. The valley is distinguished by its high edges and descends from the Tuwaiq Mountains, where its upper course lies, ending west of the town of Al Ruqaib, south of Al Dilam. It has farms and stands of talh trees.

59785616.t: Imam Turki bin Abdullah Cave (Ghar Al Shuyukh)
59785616.s: Imam Turki's Cave, also known as "Ghar Al Shuyukh" (the Elders' Cave), lies on the Al Aliyah plateau, the largest, most impregnable, highest and most valley-rich plateau of Jabal Al Yamamah. The cave is named after Imam Turki bin Abdullah bin Muhammad Al Saud, who took refuge in it to shelter from the oppression of the invading Ottomans and, when the chance arose, drove them out of Najd. Imam Turki also married in this cave and had a son whom he named Jalawi, after his Jalwa (his time of withdrawal) in the cave.

59785612.s: The tower is one of the most prominent landmarks of Al-Kharj, standing at the entrance to the governorate on the Riyadh expressway. Al-Kharj Tower is 105 metres high.
59785612.b:
The tower is one of the most prominent landmarks of Al-Kharj, standing at the entrance to the governorate on the Riyadh expressway. Al-Kharj Tower is 105 metres high.

The tower has five floors, as follows.

Basement: houses the administration, technical, control and monitoring offices, the main kitchen and the electrical substation, together with the electrical and mechanical rooms for the cooling and air-conditioning units. It was badly damaged when floodwaters swept through Al-Kharj in 1424 AH (2003-2004), particularly the electronic systems, the monitoring and control systems, the alarm and fire-fighting systems, and the air-mixing units and return fans in the basement.

First floor: contains shopping and lecture halls, a reception area, a family cafeteria and an art exhibition hall.

Second floor: contains restaurants for families and for single men, as well as the viewing deck.

Third floor: a full-floor revolving restaurant (with a moving floor), plus an upper kitchen annex equipped with high-capacity refrigerators. It seats about 320 people at a time and is furnished with tables and chairs.

Fourth floor: the mechanical floor, containing the central air-conditioning equipment, the main chillers, the lift rooms, an electrical substation, cooling units and supply pumps that provide support services to the tower.

59785584.t: Mohammed bin Saad Al Obaidi Farm, Al-Kharj
59785584.s: Mohammed bin Saad Al Obaidi Farm specialises in growing strawberries and lets visitors stroll through it and pick their own. The farm also serves fresh strawberry juice and delicious strawberry jam.

59783581.t: Maghayir Shuaib - Museum of the Prophet Shuaib (peace be upon him)
59783581.s: Madain Shuaib, also called Maghayir Shuaib or Midian, is an archaeological town of houses and temples carved into rock and mountains, in the Hejaz region of western Arabia, now near a town called Al Bid' in the Tabuk region. It resembles the ruins of Al Hijr (Madain Salih), and some archaeologists believe it dates to the second millennium BC. Its inhabitants belonged to the tribe of Midian.
59783581.b:
Madain Shuaib, also called Maghayir Shuaib or Midian, is an archaeological town of houses and temples carved into rock and mountains, in the Hejaz region of western Arabia, now near a town called Al Bid' in the Tabuk region. It resembles the ruins of Al Hijr (Madain Salih), and some archaeologists believe it dates to the second millennium BC. Its inhabitants belonged to the tribe of Midian.

Midian is mentioned several times in biblical texts. The Holy Quran mentions that the Prophet Moses took refuge with its people and married into them, that the dwellings of Midian were close to the dwellings of Thamud at Al Hijr, and that God sent to the people of Midian a prophet from among them, Shuaib (peace be upon him), to urge them toward honest trade. They refused to heed his call to believe in God and give up sinful ways.

59783575.s: The wreckage of a Catalina amphibious aircraft lies on the shore of the Gulf of Aqaba near Ras Sheikh Hamid in the Tabuk region. A US military aircraft that crashed around 1960, it has become a tourist landmark and a destination for photography and adventure enthusiasts.
59783575.b: The wreckage of a Catalina aircraft lies on the shore of the Gulf of Aqaba near Ras Sheikh Hamid in the Tabuk region. It is a US military amphibious aircraft that crashed in the area around 1960, and its wreckage still rests on the beach today, having become a tourist landmark and a destination for photography and adventure enthusiasts.

59783526.s: Al Muadham Castle is a historic fortress and one of the monuments of the late Islamic period. It lies south-east of Tabuk, in the centre of Al Muadham. It was built in 1031 AH (1622 CE) during the reign of the Ottoman Sultan Osman II and stood on the Syrian pilgrimage road. It is one of the largest Ottoman forts used to watch over and protect pilgrims, and it includes the Al Muadham pond and a railway station. Four foundation inscriptions record its construction on the castle's facade.

59783521.s: Al Radm Palace lies on the western side of Tayma. It is a rectangular palace with a well at its centre, measuring 34 by 25 metres, with walls up to 3.5 metres high and sometimes up to two metres thick. The walls are reinforced with stone buttresses at the corners, in the middle and on the outside. The palace dates to the Iron Age, the first half of the first millennium BC.

59783520.s: Tayma Museum is an archaeological museum in the city of Tayma, Saudi Arabia. It was built in 1403 AH (1983 CE) and opened to visitors in 1407 AH (1987 CE).
59783520.b:
Tayma Museum is an archaeological museum in the city of Tayma, Saudi Arabia. It was built in 1403 AH (1983 CE) and opened to visitors in 1407 AH (1987 CE).

The museum has panels showing maps of the archaeological sites of Tayma and displays a collection of artefacts and ancient writings and rock inscriptions found across the region. Among the most important is the Tayma Stele, which was displayed for a time at the Louvre in Paris. The museum also has a library of specialised books along with some periodicals and bulletins, and selected finds from the excavations carried out by the Antiquities Agency in the area, arranged chronologically from the Stone Age to the Islamic era. It also has a statue resembling the Lihyanite style, with a lion's head.

59783518.s: Haddaj Well is one of the most famous wells in the Arabian Peninsula, located in the city of Tayma in north-western Saudi Arabia. A spring at its southern corner still feeds it today. The mouth of the well is wide, 15 metres (50 feet) across and 12 metres (40 feet) deep, irregular and round in shape, and lined with stones. It became a byword for generosity, and a giving man is described as "the Haddaj of Tayma". The well lies in the middle of the old town, ringed by tall palm trees, and is believed to date to the first millennium BC.
59783518.b: Haddaj Well is one of the most famous wells in the Arabian Peninsula, located in the city of Tayma in north-western Saudi Arabia. A spring at its southern corner still feeds it today. The mouth of the well is wide, 15 metres (50 feet) across and 12 metres (40 feet) deep, irregular and round in shape, and lined with stones. It became a byword for generosity, and a giving man is described as "the Haddaj of Tayma". The well lies in the middle of the old town, ringed by tall palm trees, and is believed to date to the first millennium BC.

59783434.s: Al Mudhariyah Palace, also known as Ibn Rumman Palace, stands beside the famous archaeological Haddaj Well. It was ordered and built by Prince Abdulkarim bin Ali Al Rumman, then governor of Tayma, during the first half of the last Hijri century, using stone and mud brick. The people of Tayma, men and women alike, worked together to build it, which shows their ability and endurance in building something so fine and beautiful, using natural materials available in the town. The palace has a distinctive architectural style and is a real and rare example of traditional building methods.
59783434.b: Al Mudhariyah Palace, also known as Ibn Rumman Palace, stands beside the famous archaeological Haddaj Well. It was ordered and built by Prince Abdulkarim bin Ali Al Rumman, then governor of Tayma, during the first half of the last Hijri century, using stone and mud brick. The people of Tayma, men and women alike, worked together to build it, which shows their ability and endurance in building something so fine and beautiful, using natural materials available in the town. The palace has a distinctive architectural style and is a real and rare example of traditional building methods. It has double outer walls and towers, and contains two mosques, one for winter and one for summer, a large courtyard and many inner rooms. It remained the seat of the emirate until 1398 AH, and stood for more than 100 years, resisting changes in the weather with its beauty, a witness to an important historical period in the governorate of Tayma in the Tabuk region of northern Saudi Arabia.

59783411.s: The Tayma Wall, or Old Tayma Wall, encircles the ancient city of Tayma on the western, southern and eastern sides, but not the north, which is occupied by the salt flat known as the sabkha. The wall is more than 10 to 15 kilometres long and built of stone, mud brick and clay. In places it still stands more than ten metres high, while in others it drops to about one metre. It is between one and two metres thick.
59783411.b: The Tayma Wall, or Old Tayma Wall, encircles the ancient city of Tayma on the western, southern and eastern sides, but not the north, which is occupied by the salt flat known as the sabkha. The wall is more than 10 to 15 kilometres long and built of stone, mud brick and clay. In places it still stands more than ten metres high, while in others it drops to about one metre. It is between one and two metres thick. It is the longest wall in the Arabian Peninsula and one of the oldest archaeological walls in the world. It was traditionally dated to the first millennium BC, but recent scientific research shows that it dates to the second millennium BC.

59783405.s: The wreck of the Georgios G lies off the coast of Haql governorate, in the Bir Al Mashi area. It was a Greek ship built in England in 1949 that ran aground on the coral reefs on 4 April 1978 while carrying a cargo of flour. The ship is known as the "Saudi Titanic" and has become one of the best-known landmarks on the Haql coast, set against a backdrop of high mountains.

59783402.s: Al Muwaileh Castle is a huge historic fortress near the town of Al Muwaileh in the governorate of Duba, Tabuk region. It was once a main station on the coastal Hajj road and one of the northern gateways of the late Islamic era. It was built in the reign of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent in 968 AH (1560 CE) and has stood for 400 years. Some historians regard it as one of the largest castles in Saudi Arabia, and one of the major forts on the pilgrimage route. Inside are a courtyard, a mosque and a well, and the courtyard is surrounded on all sides by units built to serve pilgrims. The castle also has towers at each of its four corners.
